name: Vanthorpe Meridian Conceal Shoulder Rig
description:
Over-jacket shoulder harness in black vegetable-tanned synthetic leather, cut narrow and flat to disappear under a blazer or coat. Main holster sits high under the left arm with a magnetic retention snap; a counterweight pouch on the right holds spare charge packs or a secondary piece. All hardware is matte black — no shine, no jangle.

Straps cross at the upper back via a low-profile X-brace that accommodates spinal rig hardware through a split-rail channel. The whole rig weighs 340 grams unloaded. Favored by Tier 4 specialists who need to carry without advertising it.
functionality: Magnetic snap retention allows one-handed draw. Counterweight pouch balances the load and accepts secondary weapon or charge packs. Split-rail back channel routes cleanly over spinal augmentation rigs. Strap tension is micro-adjustable for chrome arm fittings. Sits flat enough to remain undetectable under a structured jacket.
what_it_says: This person is armed, doesn't want you to know it, and has enough resources to do it elegantly.
worn_by: junior executives in hostile negotiation roles
story_hooks: A counterweight pouch is found to contain a chip with encrypted comms — not weapons-related at all, suggesting the rig is being used as a dead drop carrier.
Vanthorpe's latest batch has a manufacturing defect in the magnetic snap that causes it to partially disengage under strong electromagnetic fields — common near MagRail stations.
A character is given this rig by a contact who says it belonged to someone who 'won't be needing it' — the previous owner's biometric trace is still warm in the microfiber lining.
